meta.title: Clocklings: Learn to Tell Time App for Kids
meta.description: Clocklings is a telling time app for kids. Children learn to read an analog clock step by step with a playful companion, from o'clock to exact minutes. Coming soon to Android.
meta.ogDescription: Learn the analog clock step by step, earn stars and dress up your very own companion.
meta.suggestText: This page is also available in English.
meta.ogImageAlt: Clocklings companions next to a rainbow clock

hero.title: Telling time is more fun with a friend
hero.lead: Clocklings turns the analog clock into a playful adventure. Kids learn step by step, practise reading and setting the clock, earn stars and dress up their very own companion.
hero.noteAfter: once, with no ads and no subscription.
hero.stageLabel: A Clocklings companion standing next to a rainbow clock that shows the current time

companions.title: Pick a companion to learn with
companions.lead: Nine friends, each with their own style. Your companion cheers you on, celebrates every star and loves trying on new outfits.
companions.hint: Your pick follows you around this page, even into the mini lesson.

how.title: Small steps, big smiles
how.lead: Clocklings guides kids from their very first “o'clock” all the way to reading exact minutes.

learn.title: Learn
learn.text: Friendly lessons show what the hands do, with animated demos and a narrator who reads everything aloud.

practise.title: Practise
practise.text: Read the clock, then set it yourself. A gentle hint helps after a mistake, so nobody gets stuck.

stars.title: Earn stars
stars.text: Every level can earn up to three stars. Play again any time to beat your best.

dress.title: Dress up
dress.text: Stars unlock hats, crowns, scarves and more. Over 140 outfit pieces wait in the wardrobe.

journey.whole: The long hand points straight up to 12. Read the short hand and you know the hour.
journey.half: The long hand has gone halfway around to 6. The short hand sits between two numbers.
journey.quarter: Quarter past at 3, quarter to at 9. The clock face splits into four easy slices.
journey.five: Every number is worth five minutes. Count in fives as the long hand travels.
journey.exact: The little marks are single minutes. Count to the last five, then add the rest.
journey.day: The short hand goes around twice a day. 15:30 is the same as half past three in the afternoon.

try.title: A tiny taste of practice
try.lead: Five quick tasks with whole and half hours, just like the first levels in the app. Ready?
try.more: The app keeps going with quarter hours, five minutes, exact minutes, the 24-hour day and a speedy Minute Challenge.

explore.title: Explore
explore.text: Spin the hands freely and hear what time it shows.

together.title: Play Together
together.text: One sets a time, the other guesses. Then swap turns.

challenge.title: Minute Challenge
challenge.text: How many clocks can you read in sixty seconds?

styles.title: Clock styles
styles.text: Rainbow, Space, Ocean, Forest and more. Or design your own.

voice.title: Read aloud
voice.text: A friendly narrator guides little ones who are still learning to read.

languages.title: Seven languages
languages.text: English, Finnish, Swedish, German, French, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese.

outfits.title: Every star is a little reward
outfits.lead: Crowns, wizard hats, fairy wings and party hats unlock as kids collect stars. Each companion also comes in four colours.
outfits.point1: Over 140 outfit pieces across nine companions
outfits.point2: Stars are never spent, so rewards stay unlocked
outfits.point3: Name your companion and make it truly yours

parents.title: Made with care, built to last

kind.title: Kind to every learner

free.title: Free

full.title: Full version
full.point1: All lessons, from o'clock to exact minutes

learnMore.title: Teaching the clock at home or at school?
learnMore.lead: Our step-by-step guide explains how to teach a child to tell time, and the free printable worksheets give extra practice away from the screen.

faq.title: Good to know
faq.a1: Children who are starting to learn the analog clock. Lessons begin with what the two hands do, so no earlier knowledge is needed.
faq.q2: Which devices does it run on?
faq.a2: Android phones and tablets running Android 8.0 or newer. It also adapts to foldables and larger screens.
faq.q3: Is there an iPhone or iPad version?
faq.a3: Not yet. Clocklings launches on Android first.
faq.a4: No. The free part stays free for as long as you like. Upgrade only if your child wants more.
faq.q5: Does my child need to read?
faq.a5: Not really. Instructions, hints and times can be read aloud, and the companion shows how things work.
faq.a6: Yes. A setting switches between 12-hour and 24-hour time, and a final lesson explains how the hours of the whole day work.

js.bubbleFirst: Look at the clock. Which time does it show?
js.bubbleSet: Drag the hands, or use the arrow buttons. Then press Check.
js.hintReadWhole: Look at the long blue hand. When it points straight up to 12, it's something o'clock.
js.hintReadHalf: The long blue hand points down to 6. That means half past.
js.hintReadHourHalf: At half past, the short pink hand sits between two numbers. Which one did it just pass?
js.hintReadHour: The short pink hand shows the hour. Which number does it point to?
js.hintSetMinute: Check the long blue hand. It points to 12 for o'clock and to 6 for half past.
js.hintSetHour: The long hand is right! Now look at the short pink hand. It shows the hour.
js.revealRead: It's {time}. You'll get the next one!
js.revealSet: This is {time}. See where both hands point?
js.resultUnlock: In the app, stars unlock new outfits for your companion.
js.practiceClock: Practice clock. Read the time and choose an answer.
js.sliderLabel: Clock hands. Use the arrow keys to move them by half an hour.
